title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 310
paragraphs: Against the gnats, which are very abundant, they have contrived as follows. Those who dwell above the fen-land are helped by the towers, to which they ascend when they go to rest, for by reason of the winds the gnats cannot fly up high. But those who dwell in the fen-land have contrived another way instead of the towers, and this is it. Every man of them has got a casting net, with which by day he catches fish, but in the night he puts it to the following use. He places the casting-net around the bed in which he sleeps, and then creeps in under it and goes to sleep; and the gnats, if he sleeps wrapped up in a garment or linen sheet, bite through these, but through the net they do not even attempt to bite.
